name: of, in "at the end of"
note: One word in one phrase: " of" after "the end", and more weakly after "the middle".

name: the comma between two adjectives
note: "A big, friendly dragon": the comma after a first adjective. Its direction raises the logits of more adjectives.

name: each, in "next to each other"
note: It waits for "other": the word "each" after "next to".

name: can: the container
note: "A can of paint", and the first piece of "canvas" and "canoeing". It also fires, more weakly, on "can't" and on "Can" opening a question: the meanings of the written word are not fully apart.

name: can: being able
note: "So we can enjoy": the verb after "we", with "will" and "could" beside it.

name: right: at once
note: "Come down right now!"

name: right: proper
note: "In their right place", "its rightful place"; "right away" sits here too.

name: play: an instrument
note: "Wanted to play the flute": the word "play" where what follows is a violin or a flute.

name: play: with someone
note: "A friend to play with", "no toys to play with".

name: like: as if
note: "It felt like flying": "like" after "felt".

name: like: the same as someone
note: "Brave like Anna". "Than" fires it too: it is the word that opens a comparison.

name: to: back to a place
note: "Went back to the beach": the "to" of a return.

name: to: in order to
note: "Dug a hole to hide the treasure": the "to" of a purpose.

name: to: showed it to someone
note: "Showed the folder to his mom": the "to" of giving and showing.

name: and: between two actions
note: "Running and jumping". Its direction raises the logits of verbs ending in -ing.

name: and, or: between two qualities
note: "Hot or cold", "dirty and wet".

name: the subject of a sentence
note: Names and pronouns that open a sentence, strongest on a story's very first word. It raises verbs: "smiled", "wanted", "said". It is dense: look at its share of tokens.

name: a verb waiting for its object
note: "Fun to bury ...": after a verb that takes an object, it raises "him", "the", "their", "them".

name: to, before a verb
note: "Something fun to do": it raises "play", "make", "explore", "share".

name: whose: his, her, their, my
note: The possessive before a noun, whichever word it is.

name: the first word of a speech
note: "Watch me!": the word after an opening quotation mark.

name: said, says, asked
note: The verb that follows a speech, most strongly when the speaker comes before it: "her grandpa said".

name: the ending -ly
note: "Proudly", "harshly", "carefully": how something is done.

name: many, some, more, a lot of
note: Words of quantity. It raises plural nouns: "times", "questions", "vegetables", "animals".

name: the kitchen
note: Kitchen, oven, stove, fridge, drawer, cupboard.

name: where a story is set
note: Forest, town, woods, village, jungle, most strongly in a story's first sentence: "in a thick forest".

name: river, pond, lake, road, bridge
note: Water and ways across a landscape.

name: parts of a body
note: Foot, hand, head, nose, paw, legs. Its strongest examples are "foot" inside "footprints" and "footsteps".

name: boat, ship, sail, kite, plane
note: Things that sail and fly.

name: colors
note: Red, blue, green, yellow, before a noun. At a tenth of its peak it also takes "round" and "fake".

name: a bad feeling
note: Troubled, frustrated, worried, scared, hurt, sorry.

name: shouting
note: Shout, bark, scream, yell, in every form of the verb.

name: a name, when it is given
note: "A small bird named Chirpy": the name at the moment a character receives it.

name: Once: a story's first word
note: The first token of a story, and little else.

name: who the story is about
note: "One day, a boy named Tim": boy, girl, dog, cat, at the moment they are introduced.

name: the story has just begun
note: It fires on about a quarter of all tokens, most in a story's first sentences, and lowers the words of endings: "moral", "thanked", "relieved". Too dense to be a feature of any one thing.

name: the lesson at the end
note: "Learned a valuable lesson".

name: never again: the promise
note: "I won't touch you again", "they will never do it again": the resolve that closes a story. It raises "again".

name: the last full stop of a story
note: The period after which nothing follows: its direction raises the mark that begins the next document.

name: know, thought: a question follows
note: "Didn't know what": it raises "what", "about", "why", "how".

name: the comma before "but"
note: A comma after a finished clause; its direction raises "but".

name: Can: a request begins
note: "Can I help you?": "Can", "can" and "Please" at the start of asking.

name: z in zigzag; Ann; spin; wheel
note: Its strongest examples are the letter z inside "zigzag" and "pretzel". Lower down it fires on "Ann", "spin", "wheel". We find no one meaning.

name: weak and everywhere
note: It fires on one token in twenty, never strongly, on things that are being described. We have no reading of it that we trust.
